newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jardine Fleming denies scandal prompted shakeup.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Fleming denies scandal prompted shakeup.

text.p: A spokesman at Jardine Fleming Holdings Ltd in Hong Kong denied that the retirement of the company's chairman and a radical corporate shake-up was connected to a recent trading scandal at Jardine Fleming's investment management subsidiary.
"The answer is no," a company spokesman said.

Regulators hit Jardine Fleming with a fine of 700,000 pounds and withdrew the authorisation of its London-based fund company last month following revelations of the late allocation of trades by a senior fund manager in Hong Kong.
The company volunteered to pay US$19.3 million to disadvantaged clients.
Alan Smith has retired as chairman and will be replaced by managing director, Henry Strutt.

Director Robert Thomas has resigned from the board following the withdrawal of his registration in both London and Hong Kong. He resigned earlier as chief executive of both fund management subsidiaries, Jardine Fleming Investment Management and Jardine Fleming Asset Management.
Jardine Fleming has also created a new supervisory board as part of a new two-tier board structure.
